blocking.section: Binary upgrades > Kubernetes Drain and restart; Binary upgrades > Node count during upgrades; Verification runbook
blocking.issue: This is a regression from the L3-6 fix. Each Kubernetes step now replaces one zone's share of Pods. The worked example therefore upgrades a 1,000-Node Cluster at 10% per 45 s, finishing in 7.5 minutes. Node count during upgrades says derived-ceiling Clusters MUST upgrade at most 10% of Nodes per 10 minutes, about 100 minutes per Cluster. The document gives T4 operators no way to pace a StatefulSet RollingUpdate to that rate. The runbook also requires `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes` to drop at most 10% during any upgrade, which a one-zone step of about 33% breaks even on declared-ceiling Clusters. A T4 operator cannot follow both rules, and the only worked example breaks the MUST.
blocking.evidence: Line 204: "derived-ceiling Clusters MUST upgrade at most 10% of Nodes per 10 minutes (target), about 100 minutes per Cluster (hypothesis); declared ceilings ... need no pacing." Line 278: "Each step replaces up to `maxUnavailable` Pods, M, one zone's share at minimum scale (target) ... derived-ceiling Clusters also pace as [above]". Line 282: "Example      N = 1,000, minReplicas 300, three zones: M = 100, 10 steps, 7.5 min   (hypothesis)". Line 435: "| During any upgrade | `ruralz_control_cluster_nodes`; ... | Drops at most 10% (target); no breaker opens |"
blocking.fix: In Kubernetes Drain and restart, say that the chart's RollingUpdate cannot pace to 10% per 10 minutes. On T4, a derived-ceiling Cluster therefore MUST declare per-Node ceilings before an image change. Alternatively, add an Open question owned by deployment-topologies for a paced Node update, and keep the MUST until it closes. Label the 7.5-minute example "declared ceilings". Scope the runbook row, and the count criteria in V-3 and V-5, to derived-ceiling Clusters, for example "Derived-ceiling Clusters: drops at most 10% (target); declared-ceiling T4: drops at most M Nodes per step".

blocking.section: Rollback (table row 'Ruralz Control before finalize'; Figure 4 r6)
blocking.issue: The rollback before finalize replaces only replicas and never mentions regional relays. Control plane upgrades step 3 upgrades relays to N before finalize, and the Release skew table puts a relay newer than the replicas outside policy. An operator who follows the row after relays reached N returns every replica to N-1 while the relays stay at N. That breaks the skew policy this document must match, and Release rule 5 names relays in the rolling return.
blocking.evidence: Line 419: "| Ruralz Control before finalize | Replace each N replica with N-1, one at a time, leadership moved off first | Confirm `/readyz` on 9902 and Raft catch-up | None |"; Figure 4: "r6[\"Replace replicas back to N-1, one at a time\"]"; line 326: "3. **Regional Ruralz Control relays**, Planned (M4), one at a time". Release skew table, relay row, Outside policy: "N-2; N-1 after finalize; newer than the replicas"; Release rule 5: "Before finalize, returning a replica or relay to N-1 is a rolling step."
blocking.fix: Change step 1 of that row to "Return each relay at N to N-1, one at a time (Planned (M4)), then replace each N replica with N-1, one at a time, leadership moved off first". Keep step 2 as is and add "and every relay" to it. Update the r6 label to "Relays, then replicas, back to N-1, one at a time".

non_blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover; Guarantees (ZG-3); V-3
non_blocking.suggestion: The CBPF swap covers the accept queue but not half-open handshakes. A SYN that reached the old listener just before the swap completes after `close()`, and without `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1` the final ACK finds no request socket and is reset. That conflicts with ZG-3 and with V-3's 'zero reset connections'. After step 5, keep the old listeners accepting for a short bounded window (for example until their SYN-RECV count is zero, capped in seconds (target)). Alternatively, make `tcp_migrate_req` a complement rather than an alternative (see foundation amendment).
Change 'Nodes already on N?' to 'Any Node on N?'. As written, a Cluster with only some Nodes on N can take the 'no' branch and restore an N-1 Control Store behind N Nodes.

non_blocking.section: Rollback (row 'Ruralz Control after finalize, Nodes at N')
non_blocking.suggestion: Step 1, 'steps 1 and 2 of the rollback-limit row', packs a Rollout start, an optional approval and a wait into one cell. Spell it out as "`ruralz rollout start` of the last digest without N-only fields to every Cluster, each reaching `complete`" so the row reads as three concrete actions.

non_blocking.section: Guarantees (Drain glossary row) and Drain timeline defaults
non_blocking.suggestion: The pack's Drain definition says 'readiness fails', but a handover Drain never serves a 503. Add one clause under the table: 'in a handover, readiness moves to the new process instead of failing (step 6)'. This also keeps Scalability's '/readyz fails during Drain' consistent.
Tag the '60 s timeout' in the Figure 1 alt branch with (target), as step 4 already does. The style guide requires the tag on the same line.

Two sentences are hard for operators to parse. In 'within the 60 s ACK timeout (target) while that timeout is under 23 s', 'that timeout' means the largest Plugin `limits.timeout`, so name it. The sentence starting 'An `all-at-once` Rollout, or file-mode Nodes sharing a source, reach a third activation together, a rollback and re-rollout sufficing' needs a subject-verb rewrite.
Rewrite 'the holder accepts only its active digest, has a newer candidate reloaded and reported again, and refuses an older one' as three short clauses that say who reloads what.

The body is 4,496 words against a 4,500 maximum, so any fix above will exceed the band. Make room by tightening prose elsewhere, for example the Open question rationale, rather than removing text that resolved earlier findings (L3-4 and L3-5 steps 3 to 6, the handover Drain sentence, and the rollback-limit rows).

foundation_amendments: Pack section 7, Upgrades row: '`net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` is an alternative' should read 'is a complement, or the old listener keeps accepting until its pending handshakes complete'. CBPF steering alone empties the accept queue but resets connections still in SYN-RECV on the closing listener, so zero-reset claims such as ZG-3 need one of the two.
